Subject: Draft DPA v3 (redline) — controller/processor and telemetry questions

Hi Chloe —

Thanks for walking the Blueforge team through Redwood last week. Attached is our redline to the DPA (Blueforge_DPA_v3_redline.pdf). A few high-level asks that we want to make sure are aligned before routing for signature: 

- Role clarity: we currently list Blueforge as controller and Redwood as processor. Please confirm you’re comfortable with that mapping and that the DPA language reflects it consistently (esp. in section 1 and the definitions).
- Telemetry & logs: we need explicit commitments around telemetry collection, retention, and the ability to request purge for customer-specific logs on demand. Can you confirm retention windows and whether telemetry will be delivered in aggregated/non-identifiable form?
- Embeddings: our privacy team flagged that embeddings may constitute personal data for some workloads. We’d like Redwood to commit to not surface embeddings in a way that allows re-identification and to provide a deletion API for embeddings derived from Blueforge data.
- Subprocessors: request to add a 30-day notification window for new subprocessors and an option to object.
- Cross-border transfers: we prefer SCCs (Standard Contractual Clauses) and a completed DTIA; please confirm Redwood’s approach for EU transfers.

We’d like to get to DocuSign this week if possible. Attaching the redline — let us know preferred signatory and routing.

Best,
Anika
Head of Privacy — Blueforge Systems

Subject: Re: Draft DPA v3 (redline) — comments and suggested language

Chloe / team —

I reviewed the Blueforge redline and have the following summary and recommended edits (inline changes will be shared separately):

1) Roles / Definitions — Controller vs Processor
- We are comfortable with the two-party mapping (Blueforge controller, Redwood processor) provided we clarify certain processing activities where Redwood acts as a subprocessor (e.g., cloud infra) and where customers maintain control (model prompts/labels).
- Suggested addition: an explicit definition of "Customer Data" that includes embeddings and derivatives but carves out aggregated telemetry (see below).

2) Telemetry & Logs
- We should commit to providing only aggregated telemetry by default (latency, token counts, error rates) and not per-user identifiable logs unless explicitly enabled via a paid support plan.
- Retention: propose default retention of 90 days for non-identifying telemetry, with the ability for customers to request purge of account-specific logs within 5 business days.
- Audit: we will not provide raw request/response logs containing PII unless compelled by law.

3) Embeddings
- Embeddings may be PD under certain jurisdictions. Recommend language that: (a) classifies embeddings as part of Customer Data; (b) commits Redwood to support deletion of embeddings on request; and (c) prohibits Redwood from using customer embeddings for model training unless explicitly authorized in writing.

4) Subprocessors
- Counter-propose a 30-day notice window but limit customer objection to material changes in subprocessor scope (not routine infra swaps). Provide a vendor roster and promise to notify changes via email and a dedicated notice portal.

5) Cross-border transfers
- We can sign SCCs and will provide a completed DTIA. Note: SCC execution requires operations to agree to specific subprocessors and data flows.

Next steps: Priyom / Aditya — can you confirm feasibility of 90-day retention, purge within 5 business days, and an embeddings deletion API? If product can meet that, I will prepare a final redline that accepts Blueforge’s request with the edits above and include SCCs in the execution pack.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Draft DPA v3 (redline) — product feasibility notes

Quick update from product/engineering:

- Telemetry: we already emit aggregated telemetry (latency, requests per minute, token counts) into our analytics pipeline. We can switch Blueforge to an EU-only telemetry bucket and default to 90-day retention. Purge of account-specific logs: we can implement a purge job and commit to a 5 business day SLA for removal of non-essential traces.
- Embeddings: embeddings derived from customer inputs are stored as Customer Data in our vector store. We can provide a deletion API for embedding records and mark the default retention as 90 days unless otherwise contracted. We can also add a flag to disable embedding retention for new projects.
- Data residency: we can pin Blueforge workloads to EU region and avoid cross-border replicas for production data.
- Subprocessors: updating the vendor roster is operations work; notifications can be automated to customers via the Dev Portal.

I’ve attached an export-control checklist that Blueforge asked for — it includes the infra and subprocessors we commonly use.

Priyom Das
Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
